argmax.description: All tensors are contiguous on the current CUDA device, with fixed dtypes; all outputs are fresh and no input is mutated. The selection portion of accepted finish_token, isolated as its own proof target. Inputs: BF16 logits [248320], int prompt length P, int steps S, int position t; P,S>=1, P+S-1<=12, 0<=t<12. Returns a rank-zero int64 best index. When 0<=t-P+1<S, starts at index zero and scans 1..248319 serially, updating only when !isnan(value) && (isnan(next) || next>value). Therefore the first NaN wins, otherwise the first maximum wins, including signed-zero ties. Outside the destination range the accepted branch does not read logits and best remains zero. Both branches are scheduled for every one of the original 12 finish calls; no upstream approximation or cross-implementation argmax equivalence is assumed.

embedding_rope.description: All tensors are contiguous on the current CUDA device, with fixed dtypes; all outputs are fresh and no input is mutated. The lane-zero setup at the start of each active decode_token. Inputs: BF16 embedding table [248320,1024], BF16 prompt embeddings [P,1024], int64 current tokens [S], int position t with 0<=t<P+S-1<=12. Prompt positions copy their pre-embedded row; generated positions look up tokens[t-P] (index in [0,248320)). Returns BF16 residual [1024], BF16 cosine [32], BF16 sine [32]. Uses the accepted configuration-only hexadecimal frequencies, __fmul_rn(float(t), frequency), cosf/sinf and BF16 rounding. RoPE outputs are immutable explicit inputs to all six attention blocks at this position; token and history state remain bound to their most recent producer.

final_norm_projection.description: All tensors are contiguous on the current CUDA device, with fixed dtypes; all outputs are fresh and no input is mutated. The final iteration of the accepted decoder loop, separate from selection. Inputs: BF16 tied vocabulary weights [248320,1024], BF16 final norm weights [1024], BF16 last-layer residual [1024]. Returns BF16 pre-final-normalization hidden [1024] and every BF16 vocabulary logit [248320]. Hidden is the value the accepted finish_token stores in history, not the normalized vector. Preserves the 1024-element width-four RMS reduction, epsilon, 1+weight scale, intermediate rounding and forward-K WMMA FP32 accumulation. Ordinary work is serial lane zero. Equality of selected indices for approximately related logits is not asserted; that is a separate argmax stability and composition obligation.

full_attention_decoder.description: All tensors are contiguous on the current CUDA device, with fixed dtypes; all outputs are fresh and no input is mutated. One complete full-attention decoder block. Inputs: BF16 layer weights [18352640], BF16 residual [1024], BF16 complete old KV state [C*1024], BF16 cosine [32], BF16 sine [32], int position t (1<=C<=12, 0<=t<C). KV layout is K[2,C,256] then V[2,C,256]. Returns BF16 residual [1024] and complete new KV state [C*1024], including all past and unused future slots. Includes RMS norm, Q/gate/K/V projections, per-head Q/K norm, rounded RoPE, KV insertion, causal scores and softmax, gated attention value product, output projection/residual and the complete normalized gated MLP/residual. The t==7 variant retains both accepted attention WMMA products (eight keys); all other positions retain serial dot reductions and four serial value partials, including the t==0 multiplication special case. Softmax comparison and XOR reduction order, BF16 rounding, projection WMMA tile order, and the two 1792-wide MLP partials are unchanged. Only matrix operations/operand loads use the warp; ordinary work stays in lane zero. Weights, RoPE, position and all mutable state are explicit, with no layer-number code.

initialize.description: All tensors are contiguous on the current CUDA device, with fixed dtypes; all outputs are fresh and no input is mutated. The accepted initialize_state kernel, not an invented prologue. Inputs: BF16 embedding table [248320,1024], int64 prompt [P], int steps S. Preconditions: P,S>=1, C=P+S-1<=12, prompt indices in [0,248320). Returns BF16 prompt embeddings [P,1024], BF16 zero convolution/KV cache [442368+C*6144], FP32 zero recurrent state [4718592], int64 zero tokens [S], BF16 zero history [S,1024]. Convolution occupies 18 contiguous 24576-element slices; recurrent state has 18 contiguous 262144-element slices. The cache tail holds 6 KV slices of C*1024 elements. The schedule carries each slice independently, including untouched positions; immutable embeddings remain explicitly bound to this occurrence. Original inactive decode calls (position>=C) only copy cache/recurrent state, do not change hidden/logits, and have no later state reader; these dead identity transfers remain in trace.cu, not invented schedule operations.

recurrent_decoder.description: All tensors are contiguous on the current CUDA device, with fixed dtypes; all outputs are fresh and no input is mutated. One complete recurrent decoder block, parameterized by a BF16 layer-weight slice [21555360], BF16 incoming residual [1024], BF16 old convolution state [24576], FP32 old recurrent state [262144]. Returns the BF16 residual [1024], all updated convolution state [24576], and all updated FP32 recurrent state [262144]. Includes input RMS norm, QKV/Z/beta/decay projections, four-tap convolution and SiLU, rounded Q/K normalization, 16-head recurrent update, gated output norm/projection, residual addition, post-attention RMS norm, and gated MLP/residual. Every original explicit round, FMA, contiguous_sum tree and recurrent_sum tree is retained. Projections use one 32-thread WMMA warp (BF16 operands, FP32 accumulator), forward K=16 tiles; the MLP down projection combines two 1792-wide partial sums before BF16 rounding. All ordinary arithmetic stays in lane zero. Layer weights are explicit views with schedule offsets; time dependence is entirely in the explicit convolution and recurrent inputs. Other layers' live state and RoPE remain bound to their own producers, never overwritten by this block.

token_history_update.description: All tensors are contiguous on the current CUDA device, with fixed dtypes; all outputs are fresh and no input is mutated. The existing copy/scatter portion of accepted finish_token, split only to isolate argmax verification, not an invented epilogue. Inputs: int64 old tokens [S], BF16 old history [S,1024], BF16 current hidden [1024], rank-zero int64 selected index, int prompt length P, int position t; S,P>=1, P+S-1<=12, 0<=t<12. Returns fresh complete int64 tokens [S] and BF16 history [S,1024]. At destination t-P+1, stores selected and hidden; all other entries are copied in the accepted serial loop order. Prefill and trailing inactive destinations copy the entire state unchanged. The schedule retains all 12 calls, and the latest actual final_norm_projection outputs supply the unchanged hidden/logits after active decoding ends.
